title.zh: 卷三十三 蜀書三 後主傳
title.en: Volume 33: Book of Shu 3 - Biography of the Later Lord
title.raw: 卷三十三 蜀書三 後主傳 Volume 33: Book of Shu 3 - Biography of the Later Lord

sentences.zh: 後主 劉禪

translations.literal: The Later Lord, Liu Shan.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord: Liu Shan.

sentences.zh: 建興元年夏，臧柯太守朱褒擁郡反。

translations.literal: In the summer of the first year of Jianxing, Zhu Bao, the Administrator of Zangke, seized the commandery and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: That summer of 223, Zhu Bao, prefect of Zangke, rose in revolt and took the commandery for himself.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏氏春秋》曰：初，益州從事常房行部，聞褒將有異志，收其主簿案問，殺之。

translations.literal: The Wei shi chunqiu states: At first, Chang Fang, an aide in Yizhou, was making an inspection tour of his circuit; hearing that Bao was about to harbor disloyal intent, he seized Bao's chief clerk, interrogated him under investigation, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Annals of Spring and Autumn record that earlier, Yizhou staff officer Chang Fang, on circuit duty, heard Zhu Bao was turning disloyal; he arrested Zhu's chief clerk for questioning and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 褒怒，攻殺房，誣以謀反。

translations.literal: Bao was angry; he attacked and killed Fang, and slandered him with a charge of plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Bao struck back: he killed Chang Fang and then framed him for treason.

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮誅房諸子，徙其四弟於越雋，欲以安之。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang executed Fang's sons and relocated his four younger brothers to Yuexi, intending thereby to pacify the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang put Chang Fang's sons to death, banished four of his younger brothers to Yuexi, and meant the gesture as a conciliatory signal.

sentences.zh: 褒猶不悛改，遂以郡叛應雍闓。

translations.literal: Bao still did not reform; thereupon with the commandery he rebelled in response to Yong Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Bao refused to mend his ways and soon threw in his lot with Yong Kai, rebelling at the head of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案：以為房為褒所誣，執政所宜澄察，安有妄殺不辜以悅姦慝？

translations.literal: Your subject Songzhi submits: I consider that Fang was slandered by Bao; those in power ought to have clarified and investigated—how could there be wanton killing of the guiltless in order to please the wicked?
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi argues that Chang Fang was framed by Zhu Bao and that the court should have sorted truth from falsehood instead of executing innocents to appease a traitor.

sentences.zh: 斯殆妄矣！〉

translations.literal: This is probably false!〉
translations.idiomatic: That account is almost certainly wrong.〉

sentences.zh: 先是，益州郡有大姓雍闓反，流太守張裔於吳，據郡不賓，越巂夷王高定亦背叛。

translations.literal: Before this, in Yizhou commandery the magnate Yong Kai rebelled, banished the Administrator Zhang Yi to Wu, held the commandery and did not submit, and the Yuexi Yi king Gao Ding also rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Even before that, the great clan leader Yong Kai had risen in Yizhou commandery, shipped Prefect Zhang Yi off to Wu, refused allegiance while holding the territory, and Gao Ding, king of the Yuexi tribes, had joined the revolt.

sentences.zh: 是歲，立皇后張氏。

translations.literal: That year, an empress surnamed Zhang was established.
translations.idiomatic: The same year he took Lady Zhang as empress.

sentences.zh: 遣尚書

translations.literal: A Director of the Secretariat was dispatched
translations.idiomatic: The court dispatched a Director of the Secretariat

translations.literal: (The text supplies the character Gentleman [lang] in the office title.)
translations.idiomatic: The transmitted text inserts the character lang, marking him as a Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 鄧芝固好於吳，吳王孫權與蜀和親使聘，是歲通好。

translations.literal: Deng Zhi to consolidate friendship with Wu; the King of Wu Sun Quan with Shu made peace by marriage and exchanged envoys; that year they opened friendly relations.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Zhi was dispatched to shore up ties with Wu; Sun Quan of Wu and Shu exchanged marriage overtures and embassies, and that year the two courts formally made peace.

sentences.zh: 三年春，務農殖谷，閉關息民。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year, they devoted effort to agriculture and increasing grain, closed the passes, and rested the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 225 the court pushed farming and grain stores, sealed the frontier passes, and gave the realm a respite from levies and campaigns.

sentences.zh: 三年春三月，丞相亮南征四郡，四郡皆平。

translations.literal: In the spring, third month, of the third year, Chancellor Liang campaigned south against the four commanderies; all four commanderies were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: That March of 225 Zhuge Liang led the southern expedition; the four rebel commanderies were brought to heel.

sentences.zh: 改益州郡為建寧郡，分建寧、永昌郡為雲南郡，又分建寧、臧柯為興古郡。

translations.literal: Yizhou commandery was changed to Jianning commandery; Jianning and Yongchang commanderies were partitioned to form Yunnan commandery; and Jianning and Zangke were further partitioned to form Xinggu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou commandery was renamed Jianning; land was carved out of Jianning and Yongchang to create Yunnan commandery, and another slice of Jianning plus Zangke became Xinggu commandery.

sentences.zh: 十二月，亮還成都。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Liang returned to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang was back in Chengdu by the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 四年春，都護李嚴自永安還住江州，築大城。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year, Chief Controller Li Yan returned from Yong'an and took up residence at Jiangzhou, and built a great city wall.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 226 Li Yan left Yong'an for Jiangzhou, where he raised a major fortified city.

sentences.zh: 〈今巴郡故城是。〉

translations.literal: 〈This is the old city of Ba commandery today.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The site is the old Ba commandery city wall.〉

sentences.zh: 五年春，丞相亮出屯漢中，營沔北陽平石馬。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year, Chancellor Liang went out and encamped at Hanzhong, and built camps north of the Mian River at Yangping and Shima.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 227 Zhuge Liang moved his headquarters to Hanzhong and threw up positions north of the Han River at Yangping and Shima.

sentences.zh: 〈諸葛亮集載禪三月下詔曰：「朕聞天地之道，福仁而禍淫；

translations.literal: 〈The Zhuge Liang ji records that in the third month Shan issued an edict saying: "We have heard that the Way of Heaven and Earth is to bless the benevolent and bring calamity on the wanton;
translations.idiomatic: 〈The collected papers of Zhuge Liang preserve an edict Liu Shan issued that March. It begins: "Heaven and earth bless the humane and punish the wanton;

sentences.zh: 善積者昌，惡積者喪，古今常數也。

translations.literal: Those in whom good accumulates flourish; those in whom evil accumulates perish—this is the constant pattern from ancient times to the present."
translations.idiomatic: Those who heap up goodness thrive; those who heap up evil are destroyed—that has been the rule in every age."

sentences.zh: 是以湯、武脩德而王，桀、紂極暴而亡。

translations.literal: Therefore Tang and Wu cultivated virtue and became kings; Jie and Zhou reached the extreme of cruelty and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Tang of Shang and King Wu won the throne by moral cultivation; Jie and Zhou lost it through brutality pushed to the limit.

sentences.zh: 曩者漢祚中微，網漏兇慝，董卓造難，震盪京畿。

translations.literal: Formerly the Han mandate waned midway; the net leaked and wicked men escaped; Dong Zhuo created disaster and shook the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han house faltered, the law slackened and villains slipped through; Dong Zhuo's coup convulsed the capital.

sentences.zh: 曹操階禍，竊執天衡，殘剝海內，懷無君之心。

translations.literal: Cao Cao mounted on disaster, secretly grasped the celestial steelyard, cruelly flayed all within the seas, and harbored a heart without lord.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao climbed in on the chaos, seized the levers of state, ravaged the realm, and nursed treason against his sovereign.

sentences.zh: 子丕孤豎，敢尋亂階，盜據神器，更姓改物，世濟其凶。

translations.literal: His son Pi, a solitary stripling, dared trace the steps of disorder, stole possession of the divine regalia, changed the surname and altered the tokens, and generation after generation aided his evil.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cao Pi, a callow upstart, followed that rebel path, usurped the throne, changed the dynasty's name and emblems, and his line has fed on violence ever since.

sentences.zh: 當此之時，皇極幽昧，天下無主，則我帝命隕越於下。

translations.literal: At this time the supreme pivot was dark and obscure; the realm had no lord—then Our imperial mandate fell away below.
translations.idiomatic: The pole star went dark; the empire had no true ruler, and the Mandate of Heaven seemed to slip from our grasp.

sentences.zh: 昭烈皇帝體明叡之德，光演文武，應乾坤之運，出身平難，經營四方，人鬼同謀，百姓與能。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaolie embodied the virtue of luminous wisdom, broadly displayed civil and martial excellence, responded to the fortune of Qian and Kun, came forth from humble station to pacify disaster, managed affairs in the four directions; men and spirits alike plotted with him, and the hundred surnames granted him their ability.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaolie—my father—bore brilliant, discerning virtue, gave full scope to civil and military talent, moved with heaven's turning, rose from nothing to still the turmoil, and won the allegiance of spirits and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 兆民欣戴。

translations.literal: The myriad people rejoiced and supported him.
translations.idiomatic: The people embraced him gladly.

sentences.zh: 奉順符讖，建位易號，丕承天序，補弊興衰，存复祖業，誕膺皇綱，不墜於地。

translations.literal: Obeying the talismans and prophecies, he established position and changed the reign title, greatly received the sequence of Heaven, repaired what was broken and raised what was declining, preserved and restored the ancestral enterprise, broadly received the imperial net, and did not let it fall to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Heeding portent and prophecy, he founded our house, took a new reign title, took up heaven's succession, righted a broken age, restored our forebears' work, and caught the imperial net before it could strike the dust.

sentences.zh: 萬國未定，早世遐殂。

translations.literal: The myriad states were not yet settled when he departed early on a distant demise.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was still unsettled when he was taken from us too soon.

sentences.zh: 朕以幼衝，繼統鴻基，未習保傅之訓，而嬰祖宗之重。

translations.literal: We, being young and in the flush of youth, have succeeded to the great foundation; We have not yet studied the instruction of tutors and protectors, yet are burdened with the weight of ancestors and forebears.
translations.idiomatic: I was a child when I inherited this vast charge; I had not finished the lessons tutors give a crown prince, yet I was already yoked to the weight of the ancestral shrines.

sentences.zh: 六合壅否，社稷不建，永惟所以，念在匡救，光載前緒，未有攸濟，朕甚懼焉。

translations.literal: The six directions are blocked and closed; the altars of soil and grain are not established; We eternally ponder the reason, Our thought fixed on rescue and aid, to brighten and carry forward the former thread, yet there is nothing by which to cross over—We are greatly fearful."
translations.idiomatic: The world is choked in disorder; the altars stand insecure. I search constantly for a way to rescue the state, to brighten my father's legacy, and I have found no bridge across—this terrifies me."

sentences.zh: 是以夙興夜寐，不敢自逸，每從菲薄以益國用，勸分務穡以阜民財，授方任能以參其聽，斷私降意以養將士。

translations.literal: Therefore We rise early and retire late, not daring to indulge Ourself; We always follow austerity to increase state expenditure, encourage sharing and devote effort to agriculture to enrich the people's wealth, assign methods and employ the capable to join in Our hearing, cut off private interest and lower Our mind to nurture generals and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: So I rise before dawn and sleep late, deny myself ease, stint the palace to swell the treasury, urge the people to farm and share surplus grain, put the able in office and listen to their counsel, and set aside private whim to feed the army."

sentences.zh: 欲奮劍長驅，指討凶逆，硃旗未舉，而丕复隕喪，斯所謂不燃我薪而自焚也。

translations.literal: We wished to brandish the sword on a long drive, point and punish the vicious rebels; the vermilion banner had not yet been raised when Pi again met with a falling demise—this is what is called not burning Our firewood yet burning oneself.
translations.idiomatic: I meant to draw the sword and march north against the usurpers, but before our crimson banners left the pass Cao Pi died—he needed no fuel from us; he burned himself out."

sentences.zh: 殘類餘醜，又支天禍，恣睢河、洛，阻兵未弭。

translations.literal: The remaining dregs of the remnant class, again propped up by Heaven's calamity, act wildly between the Yellow and Luo rivers; obstructing arms are not yet stilled.
translations.idiomatic: What is left of that brood still struts between the Yellow and Luo, propped up by fresh misfortune in Wei, and their spears have not been laid down."

sentences.zh: 諸葛丞相弘毅忠壯，忘身憂國，先帝託以天下，以勗朕躬。

translations.literal: Chancellor Zhuge is magnanimous, resolute, loyal, and stalwart; he forgets himself and worries for the state; the Former Emperor entrusted the realm to him, to encourage Our person.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Zhuge Liang is steadfast, loyal, and bold; he sets self aside for the state. My father left the realm in his hands to brace my own weakness."

sentences.zh: 今授之以旄鉞之重，付之以專命之權，統領步騎二十萬眾，董督元戎，龔行天罰，除患寧亂，克復舊都，在此行也。

translations.literal: Now We confer on him the weight of yak-tail pennant and battle-axe, entrust to him the authority of sole command, to command foot and horse in two hundred thousand, supervise and direct the great hosts, reverently execute Heaven's punishment, remove calamity and quiet disorder, conquer and recover the old capital—it lies in this campaign.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore give him the grand marshal's insignia, plenipotentiary command, two hundred thousand foot and horse under his banner, and charge him to carry out heaven's sentence: wipe out the rebels, still the chaos, and win back the old capital—this expedition must do it."

sentences.zh: 昔項籍總一強眾，跨州兼土，所務者大，然卒敗垓下，死於東城，宗族如焚，為笑千載，皆不以義，陵上虐下故也。

translations.literal: Formerly Xiang Yu gathered one strong host, spanned provinces and combined lands; what he pursued was great, yet in the end he was defeated at Gaixia, died at Dongcheng, his kin and clan like being burned, a laughingstock for a thousand ages—all because he did not use righteousness, overbore superiors and cruelly abused inferiors.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu once commanded a mighty host and held half the empire, yet he fell at Gaixia, died at Dongcheng, and his clan went up like kindling—a jest for every age—because he trampled right order and tyrannized those below him."

sentences.zh: 今賊效尤，天人所怨，奉時宜速，庶憑炎精祖宗威靈相助之福，所向必克。

translations.literal: Now the rebels imitate his excess; Heaven and men alike resent them; to seize the season one ought to be swift; perhaps relying on the blessing of the fiery essence's ancestors' awesome spirits assisting, wherever one turns one will surely conquer.
translations.idiomatic: Today's rebels copy that folly; heaven and the people alike curse them. The moment calls for speed. With the fiery virtue of Han and the spirits of our forebears at our back, every blow must tell."

sentences.zh: 吳王孫權同卹災患，潛軍合謀，掎角其後。

translations.literal: The King of Wu Sun Quan together pities disaster and calamity; hidden armies join in plotting, pincering from their rear.
translations.idiomatic: King Sun Quan of Wu shares our grief at this evil; his troops stand ready in secret, and we will pinch the enemy from two sides."

sentences.zh: 涼州諸國王各遣月支、康居胡侯支富、康植等二十餘人詣受節度，大軍北出，便欲率將兵馬，奮戈先驅。

translations.literal: The various kings of Liangzhou each sent more than twenty persons such as the Yuezhi and Kangju Hu marquises Zhi Fu and Kang Zhi to come receive regulation and control; when the great army goes north, they then wish to lead and command horse and foot, brandishing halberds as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Kings of the Liangzhou frontier have sent over twenty nobles—Yuezhi and Sogdian lords among them—to take orders from us; when our host marches north they will spur ahead at the van with lance and shield."

sentences.zh: 天命既集，人事又至，師貞勢並，必無敵矣。

translations.literal: Heaven's mandate is already assembled; human affairs moreover have arrived; the army is correct and power joins together—there will surely be none who can oppose.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate is gathering; the human moment has come; our cause is just and our strength massed—no one can stand against us."

sentences.zh: 夫王者之兵，有徵無戰，尊而且義，莫敢抗也，故鳴條之役，軍不血刃，牧野之師，商人倒戈。

translations.literal: As for the army of a king, there is expedition but no battle; it is honored and moreover righteous—none dare resist; therefore at the campaign of Mingtiao the army did not bloody blades; at the host of Muye the merchants turned their spears.
translations.idiomatic: A true king's host goes forth to chastise, not to brawl; it is august and in the right, so none dare face it—at Mingtiao no blade was wet; at Muye the Shang warriors dropped their weapons of their own accord."

sentences.zh: 今旍麾首路，其所經至，亦不欲窮兵極武。

translations.literal: Now as the banners and standards take the road first, where they pass through, We also do not wish to exhaust arms to the utmost of military force.
translations.idiomatic: Where our standards lead, I have no wish to wage war to the last extremity."

sentences.zh: 有能棄邪從正，簞食壺漿以迎王師者，國有常典，封寵大小，各有品限。

translations.literal: If there are those able to cast aside evil and follow the correct, with basket of food and pot of broth to welcome the royal army, the state has constant statutes; enfeoffment and favor, great and small, each have grade and limit.
translations.idiomatic: Those who leave wrong for right and meet our army with food and drink will find rank and fief spelled out in the statutes, great or small according to merit."

sentences.zh: 及魏之宗族、支葉、中外，有能規利害、審逆順之數，來詣降者，皆原除之。

translations.literal: As for Wei's kin and clan, branch and leaf, inner and outer, if there are those able to gauge benefit and harm, examine the reckoning of rebellion and submission, and come to surrender, all will be pardoned and excused.
translations.idiomatic: Any member of the Cao clan, near kin or distant, who reads the tide of fortune and comes over to us will be pardoned outright."

sentences.zh: 昔輔果絕親於智氏，而蒙全宗之福，微子去殷，項伯歸漢，皆受茅土之慶。

translations.literal: Formerly Fu Guo severed kinship with the Zhi clan and received the blessing of preserving the whole lineage; Weizi left Yin; Xiang Bo returned to Han—all received the felicity of enfeoffment with bundles of thatch.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Guo broke with the Zhi and saved his whole line; Weizi left Shang; Xiang Bo went over to Han—all were enfeoffed with land."

sentences.zh: 此前世之明驗也。

translations.literal: These are clear proofs of former ages.
translations.idiomatic: History has already written the lesson in plain characters."

sentences.zh: 若其迷沈不反，將助亂人，不式王命，戮及妻孥，罔有攸赦。

translations.literal: If they sink in delusion and do not return, will assist disorderly men, do not model themselves on the king's command, slaughter will extend to wives and children, and there will be none who are pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever clings to delusion, abets the rebels, and defies this decree will die with wife and children—there will be no mercy."

sentences.zh: 廣宣恩威，貸其元帥，吊其殘民。

translations.literal: Broadly proclaim grace and might; spare their commander-in-chief; comfort their remnant people.
translations.idiomatic: Spread both kindness and terror: spare their generals where you can, and pity the common folk caught in the middle."

sentences.zh: 他如詔書律令，丞相其露布天下，使稱朕意焉。」〉

translations.literal: As for the rest according to edicts, statutes, and ordinances, let the Chancellor publish them to all under Heaven, causing them to accord with Our intent."〉
translations.idiomatic: All other details follow statute and edict: let the Chancellor publish this abroad until every corner of the realm knows my mind."〉

sentences.zh: 六年春，亮出攻祁山，不克。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year, Liang went out and attacked Qishan; he did not overcome.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 228 Zhuge Liang struck at Qishan but failed to take it.

sentences.zh: 冬，復出散關，圍陳倉，糧盡退。

translations.literal: In winter, he again went out at Sanguan, besieged Chencang, and when provisions were exhausted withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he came out through Sanguan again, laid siege to Chencang, and pulled back when his grain ran out.

sentences.zh: 魏將王雙率軍追亮，亮與戰，破之，斬雙，還漢中。

translations.literal: Wei general Wang Shuang led an army in pursuit of Liang; Liang fought with him, defeated him, beheaded Shuang, and returned to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei commander Wang Shuang gave chase; Zhuge Liang turned on him, broke his force, killed Wang Shuang, and withdrew to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 七年春，亮遣陳式攻武都、陰平，遂克定二郡。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year, Liang dispatched Chen Shi to attack Wudu and Yinping; thereupon he conquered and settled the two commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 229 Zhuge Liang sent Chen Shi against Wudu and Yinping; both commanderies fell.

sentences.zh: 冬，亮徙從府營於南山下原上，築漢、樂二城。

translations.literal: In winter, Liang moved the attendant office camp to the high plain south of the mountains and built the two cities of Han and Le.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he shifted his headquarters camp onto the plateau south of the Qinling crest and raised the twin fortresses of Hanzhong city and Lecheng.

sentences.zh: 是歲，孫權稱帝，與蜀約盟，共交分天下。

translations.literal: That year, Sun Quan declared himself emperor, covenanted alliance with Shu, and together they exchanged division of the realm under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The same year Sun Quan took the imperial title; he and Shu renewed their treaty and formally split their spheres in the Chinese world.

sentences.zh: 八年秋，魏使司馬懿由西城，張郺由子午，曹真由斜谷，

translations.literal: In the autumn of the eighth year, Wei sent Sima Yi by Xicheng, Zhang He by Ziwu, and Cao Zhen by Xie Valley,
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of 230 Wei launched a three-pronged move on Hanzhong: Sima Yi through Xicheng, Zhang He through the Ziwu defile, and Cao Zhen up the Xie Valley,

sentences.zh: 〈斜，余奢反。〉

translations.literal: 〈Xie: read with the fanqie initial yu and final she.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Commentary gloss: the graph xie is read with the yu-she fanqie.〉

sentences.zh: 欲攻漢中。

translations.literal: intending to attack Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: intending to overrun Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 丞相亮待之於城固、赤坂，大雨道絕，真等皆還。

translations.literal: Chancellor Liang awaited them at Chenggu and Chipo; great rain cut off the roads, and Zhen and the others all returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang blocked them at Chenggu and Chipo; torrential rains washed out the roads, and Cao Zhen's columns had to turn back.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏延破魏雍州剌史郭淮於陽溪。

translations.literal: That year, Wei Yan defeated Wei's Inspector of Yongzhou Guo Huai at Yangxi.
translations.idiomatic: The same year Wei Yan routed Yongzhou inspector Guo Huai for Wei at Yangxi.

sentences.zh: 徙魯王永為甘陵王，梁王理為安平王，皆以魯、梁在吳分界故也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu Yong was moved to be Prince of Ganling, and the Prince of Liang Li was moved to be Prince of Pingan—both because Lu and Liang lay on Wu's side of the partition.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong of Lu was redesignated prince of Ganling and Prince Li of Liang became prince of Pingan, since Lu and Liang lay in territory allotted to Wu.

sentences.zh: 九年春二月，亮復出軍圍祁山，始以木牛運。

translations.literal: In the spring, second month, of the ninth year, Liang again went out with the army and besieged Qishan, for the first time using the wooden ox to transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of 231 Zhuge Liang marched on Qishan again, this time supplying the army with his wooden-ox carts.

sentences.zh: 魏司馬懿、張郺救祁山。

translations.literal: Wei's Sima Yi and Zhang He relieved Qishan.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi and Zhang He of Wei raced to lift the siege at Qishan.

sentences.zh: 夏六月，亮糧盡退軍，郺追至青封，與亮交戰，被箭死。

translations.literal: In the summer, sixth month, when Liang's provisions were exhausted he withdrew the army; He pursued to Qingfeng, fought with Liang, and was hit by an arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: By the sixth month Zhuge Liang had exhausted his grain and fell back; Zhang He pressed him to Qingfeng, joined battle, and was killed by an arrow.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，都護李嚴廢徙梓潼郡。

translations.literal: In the autumn, eighth month, Chief Controller Li Yan was dismissed and banished to Zitong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: That August Li Yan was stripped of office and exiled to Zitong.

sentences.zh: 〈《漢晉春秋》曰：冬十月，江陽至江州有鳥從江南飛渡江北，不能達，墮水死者以千數。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Han Jin chunqiu states: In the winter, tenth month, from Jiangyang to Jiangzhou there were birds flying from south of the Yangzi to cross north of the Yangzi; unable to reach, they fell into the water and died by the thousands.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Han–Jin Annals of Spring and Autumn record that in the tenth month flocks tried to fly from the south bank of the Yangzi toward Jiangzhou; thousands dropped into the river and drowned.〉

sentences.zh: 十年，亮休士勸農於黃沙，作流馬木牛畢，教兵講武。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Liang rested the soldiers and encouraged agriculture at Huangsha; when the flowing horse and wooden ox were completed, he drilled the troops and lectured on martial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 232 Zhuge Liang rested his troops and promoted farming at Huangsha, finished building his 'flowing horse' supply carts to complement the wooden oxen, and put the army through maneuvers.

sentences.zh: 十一年冬，亮使諸軍運米，集於斜谷口，治斜谷邸閣。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eleventh year, Liang ordered the various armies to transport grain, assemble at the mouth of Xie Valley, and construct the Xie Valley depot lodges.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of 233 he had every column haul grain to the mouth of the Xie Valley and built granaries and relay stations there.

sentences.zh: 是歲，南夷劉冑反，將軍馬忠破平之。

translations.literal: That year, the southern Yi Liu Zhou rebelled; General Ma Zhong defeated and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: The same year the southern chieftain Liu Zhou rose; Ma Zhong crushed the revolt.

sentences.zh: 十二年春二月，亮由斜谷出，始以流馬運。

translations.literal: In the spring, second month, of the twelfth year, Liang came out by Xie Valley, for the first time using the flowing horse to transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of 234 Zhuge Liang debouched from the Xie Valley, this time using the flowing-horse carts for logistics.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，亮卒渭濱。

translations.literal: In the autumn, eighth month, Liang died on the bank of the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: He died that eighth month by the Wei River in the field.

sentences.zh: 征西大將軍魏延與丞相長史楊儀爭權不和，舉兵相攻，延敗走。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the West Wei Yan and the Chancellor's chief clerk Yang Yi, contending for power and not harmonious, raised arms and attacked each other; Yan was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yan, general who conquers the west, and Yang Yi, chief clerk of the chancellery, fell out over authority, drew swords on each other, and Wei Yan broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 斬延首，儀率諸軍還成都。

translations.literal: They beheaded Yan's head; Yi led the various armies back to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yan was beheaded; Yang Yi brought the armies back to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 大赦。

translations.literal: A great amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 以左將軍吳壹為車騎將軍，假節督漢中。

translations.literal: The General of the Left Wu Yi was made General of Chariots and Cavalry, given credentials of authority, and directed Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yi, general of the left, was promoted to general of chariots and cavalry, given the imperial baton, and put in charge of Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 以丞相留府長史蔣琬為尚書令，總統國事。

translations.literal: The Chancellor's chief clerk of the rear headquarters Jiang Wan was made Director of the Secretariat, overall presiding state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wan, chief clerk of Zhuge Liang's rear office, became director of the secretariat and took overall direction of government.

sentences.zh: 十三年春正月，中軍師楊儀廢徙漢嘉郡。

translations.literal: In the spring, first month, of the thirteenth year, Army Supervisor Yang Yi was dismissed and banished to Hanjia commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 235 Yang Yi was stripped of rank and banished to Hanjia.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，進蔣琬位為大將軍。

translations.literal: In the summer, fourth month, Jiang Wan's position was advanced to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: That April Jiang Wan was promoted to grand general.

sentences.zh: 十四年夏四月，後主至湔，

translations.literal: In the summer, fourth month, of the fourteenth year, the Later Lord arrived at Jian,
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of 236 the Later Lord traveled to Jian,

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案：湔，縣名也，屬蜀郡，音翦。〉

translations.literal: 〈Your subject Songzhi submits: Jian is the name of a county, belonging to Shu commandery, pronounced jian.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Pei Songzhi notes that Jian is a county in Shu commandery, read like jian (scissors).〉

sentences.zh: 登觀坂，看汶水之流，旬日還成都。

translations.literal: ascended Observation Slope, viewed the flow of the Wen River, and after ten days returned to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: climbed Observation Hill to watch the Min River, stayed about ten days, and returned to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 徙武都氐王苻健及氐民四百餘戶於成都。

translations.literal: The Di king of Wudu Fu Jian and more than four hundred Di households were relocated to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: More than four hundred Di households under their king Fu Jian were resettled from Wudu into Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 十五年夏六月，皇后張氏薨。

translations.literal: In the summer, sixth month, of the fifteenth year, Empress Zhang died.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhang died in the sixth month of 237.

sentences.zh: 延熙元年春正月，立皇后張氏。

translations.literal: In the spring, first month, of the first year of Yanxi, an empress surnamed Zhang was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 238 he took another Lady Zhang as empress.

sentences.zh: 大赦，攻元。

translations.literal: A great amnesty was proclaimed, and the reign title was changed.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Yanxi.

sentences.zh: 立子睿為太子，子瑤為安定王。

translations.literal: His son Rui was established as heir apparent, and his son Yao was established as Prince of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: He named his son Liu Rui crown prince and enfeoffed Liu Yao as prince of Anding.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，大將軍蔣琬出屯漢中。

translations.literal: In the winter, eleventh month, Grand General Jiang Wan went out and encamped at Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: That November Grand General Jiang Wan moved his headquarters to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 二年春三月，進蔣琬位為大司馬。

translations.literal: In the spring, third month, of the second year, Jiang Wan's position was advanced to Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 239 Jiang Wan was promoted to grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 三年春，使越巂太守張嶷平定越巂郡。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year, he ordered the Administrator of Yuexi Zhang Ni to pacify and settle Yuexi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 240 he sent Zhang Ni, prefect of Yuexi, to bring the commandery fully under control.

sentences.zh: 四年冬十月，尚書令費禕至漢中，與蔣琬咨論事計，歲盡還。

translations.literal: In the winter, tenth month, of the fourth year, Director of the Secretariat Fei Yi arrived at Hanzhong, consulted with Jiang Wan on affairs and plans, and at year's end returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of 241 Fei Yi went to Hanzhong to confer with Jiang Wan on policy and was back before the year closed.

sentences.zh: 五年春正月，監軍姜維督偏軍，自漢中還屯涪縣。

translations.literal: In the spring, first month, of the fifth year, Army Supervisor Jiang Wei supervised detached forces, from Hanzhong returned to encamp at Fu county.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 242 Jiang Wei, as army supervisor, led a detached column from Hanzhong down to garrison Fu.

sentences.zh: 六年冬十月，大司馬蔣琬自還漢中，住涪。

translations.literal: In the winter, tenth month, of the sixth year, Grand Marshal Jiang Wan himself returned from Hanzhong and took up residence at Fu.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of 243 Grand Marshal Jiang Wan left Hanzhong and established himself at Fu.

sentences.zh: 十一月，大赦。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, a great amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: November brought another general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 以尚書令費禕為大將軍。

translations.literal: The Director of the Secretariat Fei Yi was made Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi was promoted from director of the secretariat to grand general.

sentences.zh: 七年閏月，魏大將軍曹爽、夏侯玄等向漢中，鎮北大將軍王平拒興勢圍，大將軍費禕督諸軍往赴救，魏軍退。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month of the seventh year, Wei's Grand General Cao Shuang, Xuan of the Xiahou, and others advanced on Hanzhong; General Who Guards the North Wang Ping resisted at the Xingshi enclosure; Grand General Fei Yi supervised the various armies to go hasten relief, and the Wei army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month of 244 Cao Shuang and Xiahou Xuan of Wei drove on Hanzhong; Wang Ping, general who guards the north, held the Xingshi rampart; Grand General Fei Yi led the relief host; the Wei forces withdrew.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，安平王理卒。

translations.literal: In the summer, fourth month, the Prince of Pingan Li died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Li of Pingan died that fourth month.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，禕還成都。

translations.literal: In the autumn, ninth month, Yi returned to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi was back in Chengdu by the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 八年秋八月，皇太后薨。

translations.literal: In the autumn, eighth month, of the eighth year, the Empress Dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: The eighth month of 245 brought news that the empress dowager had died.

sentences.zh: 十二月，大將軍費禕至漢中，行圍守。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Grand General Fei Yi arrived at Hanzhong and carried out encirclement defense.
translations.idiomatic: That December Fei Yi reached Hanzhong to oversee the ring of frontier garrisons.

sentences.zh: 九年夏六月，費禕還成都。

translations.literal: In the summer, sixth month, of the ninth year, Fei Yi returned to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi was back in Chengdu by the sixth month of 246.

sentences.zh: 秋，大赦。

translations.literal: In autumn, a great amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn brought a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，大司馬蔣琬卒。

translations.literal: In the winter, eleventh month, Grand Marshal Jiang Wan died.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Jiang Wan died that November.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：琬卒，禪乃自攝國事。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Wei lüe states: When Wan died, Shan thereupon himself took in hand state affairs.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei Summary says that when Jiang Wan died, Liu Shan personally assumed direction of government.〉

sentences.zh: 十年，涼州胡王白虎文、治無戴等率眾降，衛將軍姜維迎逆安撫，居之於繁縣。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the Liangzhou Hu kings Bai Huwen, Zhi Wudai, and others led their masses in surrender; Guard General Jiang Wei went to welcome them, pacified them, and settled them at Fan county.
translations.idiomatic: In 247 the Qiang chieftains Bai Huwen and Zhi Wudai of Liangzhou brought their followers in; Jiang Wei, guard general, received them kindly and resettled the people at Fan.

sentences.zh: 是歲，汶山平康夷反，維往討，破平之。

translations.literal: That year, the Pingkang Yi of Wenshan rebelled; Wei went to punish them, defeated and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: The same year the Pingkang tribesmen of Wenshan rose; Jiang Wei marched against them and crushed the revolt.

sentences.zh: 十一年夏五月，大將軍費禕出屯漢中。

translations.literal: In the summer, fifth month, of the eleventh year, Grand General Fei Yi went out and encamped at Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of 248 Grand General Fei Yi moved his headquarters to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 秋，涪陵屬國民夷反，車騎將軍鄧芝往討，皆破平之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the people and Yi of Fuling dependent state rebelled; General of Chariots and Cavalry Deng Zhi went to punish them, and all were defeated and pacified.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the mixed Chinese and tribal population of the Fuling dependency revolted; Deng Zhi, general of chariots and cavalry, led the punitive force and stamped it out.

sentences.zh: 十二年春正月，魏誅大將軍曹爽等，右將軍夏侯霸來降。

translations.literal: In the spring, first month, of the twelfth year, Wei executed Grand General Cao Shuang and others; General of the Right Xiahou Ba came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 249 Wei put Cao Shuang and his faction to death; Xiahou Ba, general of the right, crossed over to Shu.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，大赦。

translations.literal: In the summer, fourth month, a great amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was declared that fourth month.

sentences.zh: 秋，衛將軍姜維出攻雍州，不克而還。

translations.literal: In autumn, Guard General Jiang Wei went out and attacked Yongzhou; he did not overcome and returned.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Jiang Wei struck into Yongzhou but could not break the Wei lines and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 將軍句安、李韶降魏。

translations.literal: Generals Gou An and Li Shao surrendered to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The generals Gou An and Li Shao went over to Wei.

sentences.zh: 十三年，姜維復出西平，不克而還。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Jiang Wei again went out to Xiping; he did not overcome and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In 250 Jiang Wei marched on Xiping again without success.

sentences.zh: 十四年夏，大將軍費禕還成都。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourteenth year, Grand General Fei Yi returned to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Fei Yi came home to Chengdu that summer of 251.

sentences.zh: 冬，復北駐漢壽。

translations.literal: In winter, he again encamped north at Hanshou.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he moved his headquarters north again to Hanshou.

sentences.zh: 大赦。

translations.literal: A great amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Another general amnesty was issued.

sentences.zh: 十五年，吳王孫權薨。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, the King of Wu Sun Quan died.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan of Wu died in 252.

sentences.zh: 立子琮為西河王。

translations.literal: His son Cong was established as Prince of Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed his son Liu Cong as prince of Xihe.

sentences.zh: 十六年春正月，大將軍費禕為魏降人郭?所殺於漢壽。

translations.literal: In the spring, first month, of the sixteenth year, Grand General Fei Yi was killed at Hanshou by Guo ? of Wei who had surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 253 Grand General Fei Yi was assassinated at Hanshou by Guo Xun, a Wei defector.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，衛將軍姜維復率眾圍南安，不克而還。

translations.literal: In the summer, fourth month, Guard General Jiang Wei again led the host to besiege Nan'an; he did not overcome and returned.
translations.idiomatic: That April Jiang Wei besieged Nan'an again but could not take it.

sentences.zh: 十七年春正月，姜維還成都。

translations.literal: In the spring, first month, of the seventeenth year, Jiang Wei returned to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei was in Chengdu by the first month of 254.

sentences.zh: 大赦。

translations.literal: A great amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: The court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 夏六月，維復率眾出隴西。

translations.literal: In the summer, sixth month, Wei again led the host out into Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: That June Jiang Wei drove another campaign into Longxi.

sentences.zh: 冬，拔狄道、

translations.literal: In winter, he took Didao,
translations.idiomatic: That winter he seized Didao,

sentences.zh: （河間）

translations.literal: (Hejian)
translations.idiomatic: The transmitted text adds the gloss Hejian for the place name.

sentences.zh: [河關]、臨洮三縣民，居於綿竹、繁縣。

translations.literal: [Heguan], and the people of the three counties of Lintao, were settled at Mianzhu and Fan counties.
translations.idiomatic: He took the people of Didao, [Heguan], and Lintao—three counties in all—and resettled them at Mianzhu and Fan.

sentences.zh: 十八年春，姜維還成都。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighteenth year, Jiang Wei returned to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 255 Jiang Wei returned to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 夏，復率諸軍出狄道，與魏雍州剌史王經戰於洮西，大破之。

translations.literal: In summer, he again led the various armies out from Didao, fought with Wei's Inspector of Yongzhou Wang Jing west of the Tao, and greatly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: That summer he marched on Didao again, met Wang Jing, Yongzhou inspector for Wei, west of the Tao River, and shattered his army.

sentences.zh: 經退保狄道城，維卻住鍾題。

translations.literal: Jing withdrew to defend Didao city; Wei halted and encamped at Zhongti.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing fell back into Didao; Jiang Wei halted his advance at Zhongti.

sentences.zh: 十九年春，進姜維位為大將軍，督戎馬，與鎮西將軍胡濟期會上邽，濟失誓不至。

translations.literal: In the spring of the nineteenth year, Jiang Wei's position was advanced to Grand General; he supervised military horses; with General Who Guards the West Hu Ji he made a rendezvous at Shanggui, but Ji failed the oath and did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 256 Jiang Wei was promoted to grand general and took command of the field armies; he and Hu Ji, general who guards the west, had agreed to meet at Shanggui, but Hu Ji never came.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，維為魏大將軍鄧艾所破於上邽。

translations.literal: In the autumn, eighth month, Jiang Wei was by Wei's Grand General Deng Ai defeated at Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: That eighth month Deng Ai, grand general of Wei, defeated him at Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 維退軍還成都。

translations.literal: Wei withdrew the army and returned to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei pulled the army back to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 是歲，立子瓚為新平王。

translations.literal: That year, his son Zan was established as Prince of Xinping.
translations.idiomatic: The same year he made his son Liu Zan prince of Xinping.

sentences.zh: 大赦。

translations.literal: A great amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty followed.

sentences.zh: 二十年，聞魏大將軍諸葛誕據壽春以叛，姜維復率眾出駱谷，至芒水。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, hearing that Wei's Grand General Zhuge Dan had occupied Shouchun in rebellion, Jiang Wei again led the host out through Lu Valley as far as Mangshui.
translations.idiomatic: In 257, when word came that Zhuge Dan of Wei had risen at Shouchun, Jiang Wei drove through the Lu Valley again and reached Mangshui.

sentences.zh: 是歲大赦。

translations.literal: That year a great amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: The year closed with a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 景耀元年，姜維還成都。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyao, Jiang Wei returned to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In 258 Jiang Wei was back in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 史官言景星見，於是大赦，改年。

translations.literal: The scribes reported that a jing star appeared; thereupon a great amnesty was proclaimed and the year was changed.
translations.idiomatic: Court astronomers reported an auspicious jing star; the throne ordered a general amnesty and adopted the reign title Jingyao.

sentences.zh: 宦人黃皓始專政。

translations.literal: The eunuch Huang Hao for the first time monopolized government.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Huang Hao began to dominate the court.

sentences.zh: 吳大將軍孫琳廢其主亮，立琅邪王休。

translations.literal: Wu Grand General Sun Lin deposed his ruler Liang and established the Prince of Langye Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu, Grand General Sun Lin deposed Sun Liang and set Sun Xiu, prince of Langye, on the throne.

sentences.zh: 二年夏六月，立子諶為北地王，恂為新興王，虔為上黨王。

translations.literal: In the summer, sixth month, of the second year, his son Chen was established as Prince of Beidi, Xun as Prince of Xinxing, and Qian as Prince of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of 259 he enfeoffed Liu Chen as prince of Beidi, Liu Xun as prince of Xinxing, and Liu Qian as prince of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 三年秋九月，追諡故將軍關羽、張飛、馬超、龐統、黃忠。

translations.literal: In the autumn, ninth month, of the third year, posthumous titles were granted to the former generals Guan Yu, Zhang Fei, Ma Chao, Pang Tong, and Huang Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: That ninth month of 260 posthumous honors were conferred on Guan Yu, Zhang Fei, Ma Chao, Pang Tong, and Huang Zhong.

sentences.zh: 四年春三月，追諡故將軍趙雲。

translations.literal: In the spring, third month, of the fourth year, a posthumous title was granted to the former general Zhao Yun.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 261 Zhao Yun received a posthumous canonization.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，大赦。

translations.literal: In the winter, tenth month, a great amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: October brought another general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 五年春正月，西河王琮卒。

translations.literal: In the spring, first month, of the fifth year, the Prince of Xihe Cong died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liu Cong of Xihe died in the first month of 263.

sentences.zh: 是歲，姜維復率眾出侯和，為鄧艾所破，還住沓中。

translations.literal: That year, Jiang Wei again led the host out at Hehe, was by Deng Ai defeated, and returned to encamp at Tazhong.
translations.idiomatic: The same year Jiang Wei tried another sortie at Hehe; Deng Ai broke him, and he fell back to garrison Tazhong.

sentences.zh: 六年夏，魏大興徒從眾，命征西將軍鄧艾、鎮西將軍鍾會、雍州剌史諸葛緒數道並攻。

translations.literal: In the summer of the sixth year, Wei on a great scale raised transport-follower masses, ordering General Who Conquers the West Deng Ai, General Who Guards the West Zhong Hui, and Inspector of Yongzhou Zhuge Xu on several routes jointly to attack.
translations.idiomatic: That summer of 263 Wei mobilized a huge host and ordered Deng Ai, Zhong Hui, and Yongzhou inspector Zhuge Xu to advance on several columns.

sentences.zh: 於是遣左右車騎將軍張翼、廖化、輔國大將軍董厥等拒之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he dispatched the Left and Right Generals of Chariots and Cavalry Zhang Yi, Liao Hua, Assistant State General Dong Jue, and others to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Shu sent Zhang Yi and Liao Hua, generals of chariots and cavalry left and right, and Dong Jue, assistant grand general for state support, to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 大赦。

translations.literal: A great amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 改元為炎興。

translations.literal: The reign title was changed to Yanxing.
translations.idiomatic: The era name was changed to Yanxing.

sentences.zh: 冬，鄧艾破衛將軍諸葛瞻於綿竹。

translations.literal: In winter, Deng Ai defeated Guard General Zhuge Zhan at Mianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Deng Ai shattered Zhuge Zhan, guard general, at Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 用光祿大夫譙周策，降於艾，奉書曰：

translations.literal: Employing the plan of Imperial Household Grandee Qiao Zhou, he surrendered to Ai and presented a letter saying:
translations.idiomatic: On the advice of Qiao Zhou, grandee of the imperial household, he capitulated to Deng Ai and sent this letter:

sentences.zh: 限分江、漢，遇值深遠，階緣蜀土，斗絕一隅，干運犯冒，漸苒歷載，遂與京畿攸隔萬里。

translations.literal: Limited and partitioned by the Yangzi and Han, encountering circumstances deep and remote, ascending by steps onto Shu soil, isolated in a single corner, interfering with fortune and offending risk, gradually dragging through years, thereupon with the capital region was separated by ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangzi and Han have long cut us off from the heartland; fate set us on this remote plateau of Shu, a pocket realm hemmed by mountains. Year after year we have pressed our luck, until we stand ten thousand li from the imperial precincts.

sentences.zh: 每惟黃初中，文皇帝命虎牙將軍鮮于輔，宣溫密之詔，申三好之恩，開示門戶，大義炳然，而否德闇弱，竊貪遣緒，俯仰累紀，未率大教。

translations.literal: Whenever I reflect on the Huangchu period, Emperor Wen ordered General Who Bares the Teeth Xianyu Fu to proclaim a warm and secret edict, extend the grace of threefold friendship, open and show the gate and door—great righteousness blazed bright—yet my deficient virtue is dim and weak; I secretly covet the thread left by those who departed; bowing and lifting my head through accumulated years, I have not followed the great instruction.
translations.idiomatic: I still recall how in the Huangchu era Emperor Wen of Wei sent General Xianyu Fu with a gracious, confidential message offering peace on three counts and holding the door open to us. The moral case was luminous, yet I—small in virtue and dull of wit—clung to my father's legacy, bobbing through the years without answering that higher teaching.

sentences.zh: 天威既震，人鬼歸能之數，怖駭王師，神武所次，敢不革面，順以從命！

translations.literal: Heaven's might having shaken, the reckoning by which men and spirits submit to capability, fearing and trembling at the royal army, wherever divine martiality halts—how dare I not change face and comply with the command!
translations.idiomatic: Now that heavenly majesty has struck and every sign—human and spectral—points to submission, I tremble before your invincible host. Wherever it halts, how could I refuse to turn about and obey?

sentences.zh: 輒敕群帥投戈釋甲，官府帑藏一無所毀。

translations.literal: I immediately ordered the host of commanders to cast aside spears and strip armor; official bureaus and treasury stores are not to be harmed in the slightest.
translations.idiomatic: I have ordered every commander to stack arms and shed armor; no government office or state store is to be touched.

sentences.zh: 百姓布野，餘糧棲畝，以俟後來之惠，全元元之命。

translations.literal: The hundred surnames are spread across the wilds; surplus grain lodges in the fields, in order to await later kindness, and preserve the lives of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: The people remain in their fields; grain still stands in the furrows, waiting for your mercy so their humble lives may be spared.

sentences.zh: 伏惟大魏布德施化，宰輔伊、周，含覆藏疾。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Great Wei spreads virtue and applies transformation; its ministers are like Yi and Zhou; it covers and conceals even sickness.
translations.idiomatic: Great Wei spreads civilizing virtue; its ministers rival the ancient worthies Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou; its mercy covers even the flawed.

sentences.zh: 謹遣私署侍中張紹、光祿大夫譙周、駙馬都尉鄧良奉繼印綬，請命告誠，敬輸忠款，存亡敕賜，惟所裁之。

translations.literal: I respectfully dispatch my privately appointed Palace Attendant Zhang Shao, Imperial Household Grandee Qiao Zhou, and Chief of the Capitals Grooms Deng Liang to present the seals and cords of succession, request a mandate and declare sincerity, respectfully offer loyal sincerity; as to life or death, command and grant—let it be as you decide.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore send my acting palace attendant Zhang Shao, grandee of the household Qiao Zhou, and chief groom Deng Liang with the seals of state to beg for terms and declare our good faith. Life or death rests in your judgment alone.

sentences.zh: 輿櫬在近，不復縷陳。

translations.literal: The bier-cart is near at hand; I will not again enumerate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: My coffin awaits me just outside the wall; I need not belabor the point.

sentences.zh: 是日，北地王諶傷國之亡，先殺妻子，次以自殺。

translations.literal: That day, the Prince of Beidi Chen, grieving the state's perishing, first killed his wife and children, next by means of this committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Liu Chen, prince of Beidi, unable to bear the fall of the kingdom, slew his wife and children and then took his own life.

sentences.zh: 〈《漢晉春秋》曰：後主將從譙周之策，北地王諶怒曰：「若理窮力屈，禍敗必及，便當父子君臣背城一戰，同死社稷，以見先帝可也。

translations.literal: 〈The Han Jin chunqiu states: When the Later Lord was about to follow Qiao Zhou's plan, the Prince of Beidi Chen angrily said: "If principle is exhausted and strength bent, disaster and defeat will surely arrive—then father and son, lord and minister ought to fight one battle with our backs to the wall, die together for the altars of soil and grain, and so meet the Former Emperor—this would be acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Han–Jin Annals of Spring and Autumn say that as the Later Lord prepared to adopt Qiao Zhou's counsel, Prince Liu Chen of Beidi burst out: "If argument and force are both spent and ruin is upon us, then let father and son, ruler and minister, make one last stand with our backs to the city wall and perish with the altars—that would be fit company for my father in the other world."

sentences.zh: 」後主不納，遂送璽緩。

translations.literal: " The Later Lord did not accept; thereupon he sent the imperial seal and cords.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord would not hear him and sent off the seals of abdication instead.

sentences.zh: 是日，諶哭於昭烈之廟，先殺妻子，而後自殺，左右無不為涕泣者。〉

translations.literal: That day, Chen wept at Zhaolie's temple, first killed his wife and children, and afterward committed suicide; those to his left and right none did not shed tears for him.〉
translations.idiomatic: He wept before Emperor Zhaolie's shrine, killed his family, and then himself; every attendant wept.〉

sentences.zh: 紹、良與艾相遇於雒縣。

translations.literal: Shao and Liang met Ai at Luo county.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shao and Deng Liang met Deng Ai at Luo county.

sentences.zh: 艾得書，大喜，即報書，

translations.literal: When Ai obtained the letter, he was greatly pleased and immediately returned a letter,
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai read the letter with delight and at once drafted a reply.

sentences.zh: 〈王隱《蜀記》曰：艾報書云：「王綱失道，群英並起，龍戰虎爭，終歸真主，此蓋天命去就之道也。

translations.literal: 〈Wang Yin's Shu ji states: Ai's returned letter said: "The royal net has lost the Way; many heroes arose together; dragons battled and tigers contended; in the end they return to the true lord—this is probably the Way of Heaven's mandate departing and approaching."
translations.idiomatic: 〈Wang Yin's Records of Shu preserve Deng Ai's answer: "When the imperial order falters, heroes rise like spring weeds; dragon and tiger wrestle until the true sovereign wins—that is simply heaven handing the mandate from one house to another."

sentences.zh: 自古聖帝，爰逮漢、魏，受命而王者，莫不在乎中土。

translations.literal: From ancient sage emperors down to Han and Wei, those who received the mandate and became kings have none not been centered in the Middle Land.
translations.idiomatic: From the sage-kings of old through Han and Wei, every house that truly received the mandate held the Central Plain."

sentences.zh: 河出圖，洛出書，聖人則之，以興洪業，其不由此，未有不顛覆者也。

translations.literal: The River issued the chart, the Luo issued the writing; the sage modeled them to raise a great enterprise—those who do not proceed by this have none who do not overturn.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River yielded its chart and the Luo its writing; the sage took them as models to build a great realm. Ignore that pattern, and ruin follows."

sentences.zh: 隗囂憑隴而亡，公孫述據蜀而滅，此皆前世覆車之鑑也。

translations.literal: Wei Xiao relied on the Long rampart and perished; Gongsun Shu occupied Shu and was destroyed—these are all overturned-cart mirrors of former ages.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiao clung to the Long passes and fell; Gongsun Shu barricaded Shu and was wiped out—history has already painted that warning in blood."

sentences.zh: 聖上明哲，宰相忠賢，將比隆黃軒，侔功往代。

translations.literal: The sage ruler is enlightened and wise; the chancellor is loyal and worthy; he will compare in flourishing with the Yellow Emperor and Xuanyuan, and match achievement with past ages.
translations.idiomatic: Our sage emperor is lucid and wise, his ministers loyal and able; their work will rival the golden age of the Yellow Emperor and match the finest dynasties of old."

sentences.zh: 銜命來徵，思聞嘉響，果煩來使，告以德音，此非人事，豈天啟哉！

translations.literal: Bearing mandate coming to chastise, I wished to hear good tidings; truly troubling the coming envoys, they announce with virtuous sound—this is not human affair; how could it be not Heaven's opening!
translations.idiomatic: I came west on imperial order hoping for good news; your envoys have brought a noble message—such timing is more than human contrivance; heaven itself has opened the way!"

sentences.zh: 昔微子歸周，實為上賓，君子豹變，義存大易，來辭謙衝，以禮輿櫬，皆前哲歸命之典也。

translations.literal: Formerly Weizi returned to Zhou and truly became a high guest; the nobleman's leopard change, righteousness resides in the Great Changes; coming language modest and humble, with ritual bier-cart—these are all canons of former sages submitting to the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: When Weizi went over to Zhou he was honored as a guest of state; the Book of Changes praises the gentleman's timely transformation. Your humble words and offer of the funeral cart match every ancient precedent for yielding to heaven."

sentences.zh: 全國為上，破國次之，自非通明智達，何以見王者之義乎！

translations.literal: Preserving the state is highest; destroying the state is next—if one is not penetratingly wise and clear-reaching, how can one see the kingly one's righteousness!
translations.idiomatic: To save the whole realm is best; to shatter it is second best—without breadth of mind, who could grasp the true king's magnanimity?"

sentences.zh: 」禪又遣太常張峻、益州別駕汝超受節度，遣太僕蔣顯有命敕姜維。

translations.literal: " Shan again dispatched Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Jun and Aide-de-camp of Yizhou Ru Chao to receive regulation and control, and dispatched Grand Coachman Jiang Xian bearing orders to command Jiang Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Liu Shan sent Minister Zhang Jun and aide Ru Chao to take orders from Deng Ai, and Grand Coachman Jiang Xian with an edict for Jiang Wei to stand down."

sentences.zh: 又遣尚書郎李虎送士民簿，領戶二十八萬，男女口九十四萬，帶甲將士十萬二千，吏四萬人，米四十餘萬斛，金銀各二千斤，錦綺採絹各二十萬匹，餘物稱此。〉

translations.literal: He also dispatched Gentleman of the Secretariat Li Hu to deliver the register of gentry and people: leading households two hundred eighty thousand, male and female mouths nine hundred forty thousand, armored generals and soldiers one hundred two thousand, clerks forty thousand, rice more than four hundred ten thousand hu, gold and silver each two thousand jin, brocade and figured silks and dyed silks each two hundred thousand bolts—remaining goods matched these.〉
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Secretariat gentleman Li Hu with the census: 280,000 households, 940,000 persons, 102,000 troops under arms, 40,000 officials, more than 4.1 million hu of grain, two thousand jin each of gold and silver, two hundred thousand bolts each of brocade and fine silks—other stores were in proportion.〉

sentences.zh: 遣紹良先還。

translations.literal: He dispatched Shao and Liang to return first.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shao and Deng Liang were sent back ahead of the main party.

sentences.zh: 艾至城北，後主興櫬自縛，詣軍壘門。

translations.literal: When Ai arrived north of the city, the Later Lord raised a bier and bound himself and went to the camp gate of the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Ai reached the north wall of Chengdu, the Later Lord came out with a coffin on a cart, his hands bound behind him, and presented himself at the camp gate.

sentences.zh: 艾解縛焚櫬，延請相見。

translations.literal: Ai loosed the bonds, burned the bier, and extended invitation to meet and see.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai cut his bonds, burned the bier, and received him as a guest.

sentences.zh: 〈《晉諸公贊》曰：劉禪乘騾車詣艾，不具亡國之禮。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Jin zhugong zan states: Liu Shan rode a mule cart to visit Ai and did not perform the rites of a perished state.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Jin Eulogies of the Dukes say Liu Shan drove a mule cart to Deng Ai and omitted the full ritual of a conquered sovereign.〉

sentences.zh: 因承製拜後主為驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon, assuming imperial writ, he appointed the Later Lord General Who Gallops Like the Piebald.
translations.idiomatic: Acting on interim authority he named the Later Lord general who gallops like the piebald horse.

sentences.zh: 諸圍守悉被後主敕，然後降下。

translations.literal: The various encirclement defenders all received the Later Lord's edict, and afterward submitted and came down.
translations.idiomatic: Every ring of Shu garrisons received the Later Lord's order before laying down arms.

sentences.zh: 艾使後主止其故宮，身往造焉。

translations.literal: Ai ordered the Later Lord to stop at his former palace; he himself went to visit there.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai let him remain in his old palace and went in person to call on him.

sentences.zh: 資嚴未發，明年春正月，艾見收。

translations.literal: Funds and strictness had not yet been dispatched; in the spring, first month, of the next year, Ai was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Before the victory bounty could be sent out, Deng Ai was arrested in the first month of the following spring.

sentences.zh: 鍾會自涪至成都作亂。

translations.literal: Zhong Hui from Fu arrived at Chengdu and created disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui marched from Fu to Chengdu and there raised a mutiny.

sentences.zh: 會既死，蜀中軍眾鈔略，死喪狼籍，數日乃安集。

translations.literal: When Hui had died, the armies and masses in Shu plundered; deaths and corpses lay strewn; only after several days were they pacified and gathered.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhong Hui's death Shu became a chaos of looting and corpses in the streets; order took several days to return.

sentences.zh: 後主舉家東遷，既至洛陽，策命之曰：

translations.literal: The Later Lord moved his whole household east; when he had arrived at Luoyang, a patent of enfeoffment ordered him, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord took his household east to Luoyang, where he received this patent of appointment:

sentences.zh: 惟景元五年三月丁亥，皇帝臨軒，使太常嘉命劉禪為安樂縣公。

translations.literal: On the dinghai day of the third month of the fifth year of Jingyuan, the Emperor faced the gallery and ordered the Minister of Ceremonies to grant a favorable mandate to Liu Shan as Duke of Anle county.
translations.idiomatic: On the dinghai day of the third month, 264, the Wei emperor held court and charged the minister of ceremonies to invest Liu Shan as duke of Anle county.

sentences.zh: 於戲，其進聽朕命！

translations.literal: Alas, advance and listen to Our command!
translations.idiomatic: Hearken, then, and receive Our word!

sentences.zh: 蓋統天載物，以咸寧為大，光宅天下，以時雍為盛。

translations.literal: In general, threading Heaven and bearing the myriad things, to take universal quieting as great; broadly dwelling over all under Heaven, to take timely harmony as flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: He who spans heaven and bears the myriad creatures counts universal peace as his greatest end; he who lights the world esteems the harmony of the seasons as his highest glory.

sentences.zh: 故孕育群生者，君人之道也，乃順承天者，坤元之義也。

translations.literal: Therefore to conceive and nourish the throng of the living is the Way of the lord of men; then to comply and receive Heaven is the meaning of Kun's origin.
translations.idiomatic: To cherish and nourish all life is the way of the true king; to bow before heaven's turning is the virtue Earth itself shows in the Classic of Changes.

sentences.zh: 上下交暢，然後萬物協和，庶類獲乿。

translations.literal: Above and below exchange smoothly; thereafter the myriad things harmonize together, and the multitude of kinds obtain nurture.
translations.idiomatic: When high and low move in concord, the myriad things thrive and every kind of creature finds its nurture.

sentences.zh: 乃者漢氏失統，六合震擾。

translations.literal: Formerly the Han clan lost the thread; the six directions quaked and were disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the Han lost the thread of rule and the realm shook with rebellion.

sentences.zh: 我太祖承運龍興，弘濟八極，是用應天順民，撫有區夏。

translations.literal: Our Grand Progenitor received the fortune and the dragon rose; he broadly aided the eight extremities; by this he responded to Heaven and complied with the people, soothing and possessing the regional Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynastic founder caught heaven's mandate like a rising dragon, brought peace to the farthest corner, answered both heaven and the people, and took the Central States in hand.

sentences.zh: 於時乃考因群傑虎爭，九服不靜，乘間阻遠，保據庸蜀，遂使西隅殊封，方外壅隔。

translations.literal: At that time your deceased father, because many heroes contended like tigers, the nine domains were not quiet, exploiting the gap and blocking the distance, preserved and occupied Yong and Shu, thereupon causing the western corner to have peculiar enfeoffment and the outer regions to be blocked and cut off.
translations.idiomatic: In those years of warlords your father seized the chance to hold the Ba–Shu fastness; the west became a separate realm and the frontier stayed closed for generations.

sentences.zh: 自是以來，干戈不戢，元元之民，不得保安其性，幾將五紀。

translations.literal: From this time on, shields and spears were not gathered; the black-headed people could not obtain peace and security for their natures—nearly going on five periods of twelve years.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since, arms have seldom been sheathed and the common folk have known no lasting peace—nearly sixty years.

sentences.zh: 朕永惟祖考遺志，思在綏緝四海，率土同軌，故爰整六師，耀威梁、益。

translations.literal: We eternally ponder Our ancestors' and fathers' bequeathed intent; Our thought is on pacifying and gathering the four seas, so that all within the soil follow the same track; therefore We thereupon arrayed the six armies and displayed might in Liang and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: We have long pondered our forebears' charge to quiet the four seas and bring every road onto one track; hence We arrayed the six hosts and showed Our majesty in Liang and Yi.

sentences.zh: 公恢崇德度，深秉大正，不憚屈身委質，以愛民全國為貴，降心回慮，應機豹變，覆信思順，以享左右無疆之休，豈不遠歟！

translations.literal: The Duke broadly exalts virtue and measure, deeply grasps great correctness, does not shrink from bending body and submitting substance, taking love of the people and preserving the whole state as noble; lowering mind and turning thought, responding to the opportunity with leopard change, turning trust and pondering submission, thereby to enjoy left and right without-bound felicity—how is this not far-reaching!
translations.idiomatic: You, Duke, have shown high principle and true rectitude; you did not scorn to humble yourself and yield the realm to spare your people. You read the moment, changed like the leopard in the Changes, chose good faith and submission, and so win unbounded blessing on every side—could any reward be more fitting?

sentences.zh: 朕嘉與君公長饗顯祿，用考咨前訓，開國胙土，率遵舊典，錫茲玄牡，苴以白茅，永為魏藩輔，往欽哉！

translations.literal: We rejoice to grant you, lord and duke, long enjoyment of illustrious emoluments; thereby to examine and consult former instruction, to open a state and enfeoff with soil, entirely following old canons; We bestow on you this black bull, wrapped with white thatch—ever be a Wei screen and support; go—revere this!
translations.idiomatic: We delight to let you, Duke, feast on rank and stipend for years to come, take counsel from the ancient models, found your fief with clods of sacred earth, and follow every precedent of investiture: here is the black sacrificial bull, bundled in white rushes—be forever a bulwark of Wei. Go, and receive it with reverence!

sentences.zh: 公其只服朕命，克廣德心，以終乃顯烈。

translations.literal: You ought respectfully to submit to Our command, being able broadly to expand the mind of virtue, thereby to complete your illustrious merit.
translations.idiomatic: Honor this charge, let your virtuous intent broaden ever further, and bring your noble service to its fitting close.

sentences.zh: 評曰：後主任賢相則為循理之君，惑閹堅則為昏暗之後，傳曰‘素絲無常，唯所染之’，信矣哉！

translations.literal: The appraisal states: The Later Lord, when he employed worthy chancellors, was a ruler who followed principle; when he was deluded by eunuch stalwarts, he was a dim successor. The tradition says, 'The plain silk has no constant hue—it takes the color of what dyes it'—truly it is so!
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shou's judgment runs thus: with good chancellors at his side the Later Lord kept to the right path; once palace eunuchs swayed him he sank into folly. The adage holds: white silk shows whatever dip it meets—his reign proved it true.

sentences.zh: 禮，國君繼體，逾年改元，而章武之三年，則革稱建興，考之古義，體理為違。

translations.literal: By ritual, when a state's lord succeeds the bodily vessel, after crossing a year he changes the reign title; yet in the third year of Zhangwu he altered it to Jianxing—examining this against ancient meaning, the substance and principle are contrary.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual expects a new ruler to wait a full year before changing the era name, yet in the third year of Zhangwu he switched to Jianxing—set against classical usage, that was irregular.

sentences.zh: 又國不置史，注記無官，是以行事多遺，災異靡書。

translations.literal: Moreover the state did not establish historians; there were no offices for annotation and record—therefore in conduct of affairs much was lost, and prodigies and anomalies were not written.
translations.idiomatic: Nor did Shu maintain court historians or a diary office, so much of what happened went unrecorded and portents were never logged.

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮雖達於為政，凡此之類，猶有未周焉。

translations.literal: Although Zhuge Liang was penetrating in conducting government, in categories such as these there was still incompleteness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang was a master of administration, yet even he left gaps like these unfilled.

sentences.zh: 然經載十二而年名不易，軍旅屢興而赦不妄下，不亦卓乎！

translations.literal: Yet for twelve years on record the reign title was not changed; armies marched time and again yet amnesties were not issued recklessly—is this not outstanding!
translations.idiomatic: For a full dozen years he left the era name untouched and refused to buy popularity with blanket pardons—few could match that discipline.

sentences.zh: 自亮沒後，茲制漸虧，優劣著矣。

translations.literal: From after Liang's demise, this system gradually declined—superiority and inferiority stood revealed.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the old discipline frayed, and the contrast could not have been clearer.

sentences.zh: 〈《華陽國志》曰：丞相亮時，有言公惜赦者，亮答曰：“治世以大德，不以小惠，故匡衡、吳漢不原為赦。

translations.literal: 〈The Huayang guo zhi states: In Chancellor Liang's time, there were those who said the duke grudged amnesties; Liang replied: "In ordering the age one relies on great virtue, not on small kindness; therefore Kuang Heng and Wu Han were unwilling to be authors of amnesties."
translations.idiomatic: The Huayang Records relate that when someone complained Zhuge Liang granted amnesties too rarely, he answered: Good government rests on broad moral sway, not petty indulgence—Kuang Heng and Wu Han likewise refused to make a habit of pardons.

sentences.zh: 先帝亦言吾周旋陳元方、鄭康成間，每見啟告，治亂之道悉矣，曾不語赦也。

translations.literal: The Former Emperor also said: 'In my comings and goings between Chen Yuanfang and Zheng Kangcheng, each time I saw them open and inform me, the ways of order and disorder were complete, yet they never spoke of amnesties.'
translations.idiomatic: My father used to say that in his talks with Chen Ji and Zheng Xuan every question of order and chaos was covered, yet neither man ever urged him to declare an amnesty.

sentences.zh: 若劉景升、季玉父子，歲歲赦宥，何益於治！

translations.literal: Like Liu Jingsheng and the father and son Ji Yu, year after year granting amnesty and forgiveness—what benefit was there to governance!
translations.idiomatic: Look at Liu Biao and the two Liu Zhangs, who pardoned year after year—what good did it do their realm?

sentences.zh: ”臣松之以為‘赦不妄下’，誠為可稱，至於‘年名不易’，猶所未達。

translations.literal: Your subject Songzhi considers that 'amnesties not recklessly issued' is indeed praiseworthy; as for 'year name not changed,' I have still not comprehended.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi adds that sparing amnesties deserves praise, but the praise for never changing the era name leaves him puzzled.

sentences.zh: 案建武、建安之號，皆久而不改，未聞前史以為美談。

translations.literal: Examining the designations Jianwu and Jian'an, both were long without change; I have not heard former histories take this as fine discourse.
translations.idiomatic: The Han used Jianwu and Wei used Jian'an for many years without fuss—no chronicler ever called that a special virtue.

sentences.zh: ‘經載十二’，蓋何足雲？

translations.literal: 'The classics record twelve'—how is it worth speaking?
translations.idiomatic: And what is so marvelous about a mere twelve-year span?

sentences.zh: 豈別有他意，求之未至乎！

translations.literal: Could there be some other meaning, and in seeking it I have not reached it!
translations.idiomatic: Unless Chen Shou meant something subtler that I have failed to grasp?

sentences.zh: 亮歿後，延熙之號，數盈二十，‘茲制漸虧’，事又不然也。〉

translations.literal: After Liang's death, the designation Yanxi, the number filled more than twenty—'this system gradually declined'—the affair is again not so.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuge Liang died, the Yanxi era ran on for more than twenty years, so the claim that institutions steadily crumbled does not quite fit either.〉
